title: Public repo ships live deployable DB with demo credentials
summary: db/custom.db is committed to a public repo, deployed as-is by npm start and .zscripts, and contains 20 users with scrypt-hashed demo password 'password123' (ada@example.org documented in README). GreenShoots org has non-null invite code. 17 e2e test joiner accounts accumulate. Deployment built from repo lets anyone log in as documented user or join the advertised org with published credentials.

evidence.description: 20 users, 3 orgs, GreenShoots invite code non-null, 17 e2e joiner accounts

affected_resource: org-scoped media, reports, notes; user accounts; invite codes
impact: Unauthorized login to demo accounts, org join with published code, member-level access to org data
source_fix: Remove db/custom.db from git (git rm --cached), add db/*.db to .gitignore, ship db/seed.db (sanitized fixture) for e2e instead. CI already materializes per run.
test_case: e2e/sec-p6.spec.ts: verify demo login is rejected; e2e suite still passes against seed.db fixture

title: Cloudinary API credential in git history
summary: Commit 51de907 (AUDIT.md line 119) contains a 27-character Cloudinary credential. Removed in 4bc0d0b but still reachable from origin/main. Credential may be rotated or revoked; verification needed.
affected_resource: Cloudinary account and assets (images, API quota)
impact: Potential unauthorized API calls, asset deletion/modification, quota depletion
source_fix: Verify credential rotation status with owner; if not rotated, revoke and rotate. History rewrite (BFG/git-filter-repo) is non-blocking if rotation confirmed.
needs_validation_blocker: Owner must confirm Cloudinary credential rotation status; credential may already be revoked
